definitions.gloss: X mark; cross mark; wrong answer mark
definitions.explanation: A cross-shaped symbol (×) used to indicate something is wrong, incorrect, or not permitted. Opposite of ○ (maru, circle mark for correct).
Colloquially used to indicate that someone has been divorced. バツイチ means divorced once.

examples.japanese: ⟦{間違|まちが}った→間違う：03036_machigau⟧⟦{答|こた}え→答え：00790_kotae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧バツ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{付|つ}く→付く：01960_tsuku⟧。
examples.english: Wrong answers get an X mark.

examples.japanese: ⟦ここ→ここ：00961_koko⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{撮影|さつえい}→撮影：04175_satsuei⟧⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧です。×⟦マーク→マーク：09478_maaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}えます→見える：01165_mieru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Photography is prohibited here. Do you see the X mark?

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧バツイチで、⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一人|ひとり}→一人：00630_hitori⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: He's divorced once and has one child.
examples.notes: [Note: バツイチ = divorced once, バツニ = divorced twice]

examples.japanese: ⟦テスト→テスト：01065_tesuto⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{三|さん}つ→三つ：02970_mittsu⟧バツ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{付|つ}いた→付く：01960_tsuku⟧。
examples.english: I got three answers wrong on the test.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駐車|ちゅうしゃ}→駐車：01466_chuusha⟧⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧バツ⟦マーク→マーク：09478_maaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}える→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: I can see the no-parking X mark.

examples.japanese: ⟦{正|ただ}しい→正しい：00893_tadashii⟧⟦もの→物：02259_mono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{丸|まる}→丸：02167_maru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧、⟦{間違|まちが}っている→間違う：03036_machigau⟧⟦もの→物：02259_mono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧バツ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{付|つ}けて→付ける：00761_tsukeru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please mark correct ones with a circle and wrong ones with an X.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧×⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なっています→なる：01970_naru⟧。
⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01293_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧バツニで、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{独身|どくしん}→独身：03486_dokushin⟧です。
examples.english: She's been divorced twice and is currently single.

examples.japanese: バツイチ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{結婚|けっこん}→結婚：02514_kekkon⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{気|き}にします→気にする：03026_kinisuru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Do you mind marrying someone who's been divorced?

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧バツイチで⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{全然|ぜんぜん}→全然：00598_zenzen⟧⟦{気|き}にしない→気にする：03026_kinisuru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: These days, many people don't mind at all if someone is divorced.

notes:
WRITING: Written as × (the symbol), バツ, or ばつ.

USAGE:
・× indicates wrong/incorrect (on tests, forms)
・× indicates prohibited/not allowed (signs)
・× indicates unavailable/closed (schedules)

SLANG:
・バツイチ (バツ{一|いち}) - divorced once
・バツニ - divorced twice
(The 'X' represents a mark crossing out one's family register)

CONTRAST:
・○ (まる) - correct, good, available
・× (ばつ) - wrong, prohibited, unavailable
・△ (さんかく) - so-so, partially correct

NOTE: In Japan, ○ means 'correct' and × means 'wrong', which is opposite to the Western ✓ (check) and ✗ (X) convention.
